papers.title: A counterexample to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a unital \(\sigma\)-weakly closed subalgebra \(\mathfrak A\) of a von Neumann factor \(\mathcal M\) of type \(\mathrm{II}_1\), whose diagonal is \(\mathfrak D=\mathfrak A\cap\mathfrak A^*=\mathbb CI\). We show that there exist uncountably many faithful normal conditional expectations from \(\mathcal M\) onto \(\mathfrak D\) with respect to each of which \(\mathfrak A\) is a maximal subdiagonal algebra. Let \(\tau\) denote the unique normalized faithful normal trace on \(\mathcal M\). The conditional expectation associated with \(\tau\) preserves this trace, whereas none of the other conditional expectations is preserved by any nonzero finite trace on \(\mathcal M\). This gives a negative answer to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras in \emph{Amer. J. Math.} \textbf{89}(1967), 578--642.

papers.title: Nuclear dimension of uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that for every discrete metric space $X$ of bounded geometry with Yu's Property A, the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ has nuclear dimension at most one. This answers in the negative a long-standing question of Winter and Zacharias on whether the nuclear dimension of $C^*_u(X)$ always equals the asymptotic dimension of $X$. Consequently, $dim_{nuc} C^*_u(X)\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ for every discrete metric space $X$, with or without bounded geometry.

papers.title: Effectively nuclear C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We study the computable content of nuclearity for $C^*$-algebras. We show that nuclearity effectivizes automatically: a presentation of a $C^*$-algebra is effectively nuclear, in the sense that the completely positive approximations witnessing nuclearity can be computed uniformly from the data they approximate, if and only if it is a computable presentation of a nuclear $C^*$-algebra, and likewise for the effectivization of the Choi--Effros form of nuclearity. The main tool is an effective version of the Arveson extension theorem: we prove that the $n$-th matrix numerical range of a tuple from a computable presentation is computably compact, uniformly in all of its data, and deduce an algorithm which converts an approximately attainable tuple of matrices into a computable unital completely positive map attaining it. A byproduct is that the computable states of any computable presentation of a unital $C^*$-algebra are weak$^*$-dense in its state space. We also prove that the Cuntz algebras $\mathcal{O}_n$ are computably categorical and obtain an effective form of Kirchberg--Phillips absorption. By contrast with the conditions above, we do not know whether every computable presentation of a nuclear $C^*$-algebra admits a computable embedding into $\mathcal{O}_2$ with a computable conditional expectation; we answer this affirmatively for commutative $C^*$-algebras, for AF algebras, and, by a dynamical argument using invariant states, for the group $C^*$-algebras of a class of amenable groups including all finitely presented residually finite ones. Finally, we show that the set of indices of computable presentations of nuclear $C^*$-algebras is $\Pi^0_2$, and that the corresponding set for c.e. presentations is $\Pi^0_2$-hard; the latter rests on a result of independent interest, namely that amenability of computable groups is $\Pi^0_2$-complete within the class of computable groups.

papers.title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
papers.abstract: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.

papers.title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
papers.abstract: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

papers.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.

papers.title: Cartesian products of groups as quantum metric spaces
papers.abstract: We provide a new class of finitely generated groups whose word-length functions give rise to compact quantum metric spaces. Kaad's recent theory of matrix compact quantum metric spaces is instrumental in obtaining this new class, and along the way we also show that any length function on an amenable group which gives rise to a compact quantum metric space in fact gives rise to a matrix compact quantum metric space, and that the corresponding result is false for the free group on two generators.

papers.title: A commuting operator self-test for exact entanglement embezzlement
papers.abstract: We show that the optimal commuting operator correlation for a variant of Coladangelo's two-player generalized nonlocal game, based on the embezzlement of entanglement, is a commuting operator self-test. Our result gives the first correlation self-test for an exact entanglement embezzlement protocol in the commuting operator framework. Because the unique optimal correlation necessitates the exact embezzlement of entanglement, the correlation is unrealizable using quantum tensor-product models, even if the local spaces are allowed to be infinite dimensional. Our proof relies on Harris' unique abstract state characterization of exact embezzlement of entanglement involving Cuntz algebras.
